revision: REVISED 2026-08-14 by the run owner after first-party logo assets were retrieved and measured. The earlier version of this file recorded zero colour values and two low-confidence third-party candidates. Both candidates are now DISPROVED as first-party values. See `measurementNote` and `contradictions`.
summary: Vauxhall's mark is red plus navy, and both values are now MEASURED from first-party PNG assets: #eb0000 for the griffin roundel and #00003a for the wordmark. No first-party colour SPECIFICATION (Pantone, CMYK, or a stated hex in a guideline) was found anywhere this run, so what is recorded here is what the brand's own published assets render, which is a different and slightly weaker claim than a published token. The two hex candidates previously carried from a fan-wiki SVG (#d7001c, #000037) do NOT match the first-party assets and must not be used. Colour ladder rungs 1 to 4 remain structurally unreachable; the values below come from a newly opened route, first-party raster assets measured pixel-wise, which sits alongside rung 3 rather than on the published ladder.

measurementNote.how: Four first-party PNG assets were fetched, verified with file(1) as genuine PNGs, and measured with Pillow 11.3.0. Only pixels with alpha > 200 were counted. Reported percentages are shares of opaque pixels.
measurementNote.colourManagement: NONE of the four PNGs carries an embedded ICC profile, so sRGB is assumed and the hex values are used as read. This is the standard assumption and it is stated because a tagged profile would change the numbers.
measurementNote.whyThisIsNotRung3: Rung 3 is a live DOM or manifest. This is neither. It is a published raster asset on a first-party host, measured directly. It beats any third-party artefact and it is dated only by its live use, not by a publication date.
measurementNote.independence: vauxhall-logo-stellantis-dam.png and vauxhall-stellantis-dam.png are the SAME artwork at different canvas sizes: identical colour proportions (80.68 / 19.32) and inked aspect ratios of 1.1753 and 1.1755. They are ONE source in two renditions and must not be counted as two independent corroborations.

Measured and viewed, it is simply the vertical lockup rendered in ONE flat colour. It is distinctly greener and lighter than the wordmark navy #00003a, so the mono variant is not just the wordmark colour reused. It resolves the red-versus-blue question rather than creating one.

disproved.wasClaimedAs: the emblem red, read out of a Wikipedia/Logopedia SVG (A4) and independently found declared in an Evans Halshaw dealer SVG (A4)
disproved.why: The first-party assets render #eb0000. #d7001c differs in every channel (215 vs 235 red, 28 vs 0 blue). It is not a rounding artefact and there is no colour profile in play that would explain it.
disproved.keepBecause: Two independent-looking third-party sources both state it, so it is the value circulating in the dealer and fan-wiki supply chain. That is worth knowing when auditing third-party Vauxhall material, but it must not populate tokens.

disproved.wasClaimedAs: the wordmark navy, same two third-party sources
disproved.why: The first-party assets render #00003a. The blue channel is 58, not 55.
disproved.keepBecause: The near-miss is diagnostic. A three-unit drift in one channel is what re-tracing or re-saving a logo through a third-party pipeline looks like, which supports the shared-ancestry reading below.

contradictions.issue: Which hue leads the current identity: red or blue
contradictions.valueB: blue, inferred from the live first-party asset filename 'verticalbluecopy'
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED BY MEASUREMENT 2026-08-14. Both are true and they were never in conflict. The full-colour master lockup is a RED griffin roundel (#eb0000) above a NAVY wordmark (#00003a). The 'blue' asset is a one-colour MONOCHROME variant of the same vertical lockup, rendered entirely in #002a42. The filename described a variant treatment, not a competing primary. Per the run's precedence rules a measurement wins on a rendered fact, and this is a rendered fact.

contradictions.issue: Whether the two third-party sources agreeing on #d7001c and #000037 constituted independent corroboration or shared ancestry
contradictions.valueA: independent corroboration: a franchised retailer's asset library is supplied through Vauxhall's dealer marketing channel, so exact agreement with the fan-wiki file would mean both descend from the real master
contradictions.valueB: shared ancestry: Wikipedia's own file history cites 'an official SVG from a Vauxhall dealer site', so both copies may descend from one dealer-supplied file and agreement proves only lineage
contradictions.resolution: RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF SHARED ANCESTRY. Both third-party sources agree exactly with each other and BOTH differ from the first-party assets. Two sources agreeing on a wrong value is the signature of one common upstream copy, not of independent access to the master. The web dimension's suspicion was correct and is now evidenced.
contradictions.consequence: The stopping rule of 'two independent sources agree' must not be applied to these two. Recorded so a later run does not re-promote #d7001c.

stillNotPublished: Any colour SPECIFICATION: no Pantone, no CMYK, no stated hex, no colour name, from any first-party source. Everything above is measured off artwork, which cannot tell you the intended spec or the print build.

A secondary or extended palette. Nothing beyond the two mark colours and the two variant treatments was evidenced. Whether Vauxhall has UI greys, accent colours or a tint system is UNKNOWN, not absent.

Any dating of these values, so they cannot be checked for staleness against the unresolved identity date.
